items_missed: No agenda statement — never framed the call ('I'll gather details, then walk you through pricing, takes 10-15 minutes'). Opened with 'are you available to go over a few things?' and jumped straight into the differentiators pitch.
No 'sound good?' style confirmation after an agenda statement.
Never used the customer's name once in a 21-minute call — the customer opened by giving it ('this is Babish') and by name-checking the rep ('Hi, Bri').
Did not probe additional rooms — garage, storage unit, balcony/patio (relevant for a 2BR apartment with packing service).
Did not ask about storage stops.
Did not ask about additional stops.
Skipped the 'pricing is super simple' opener — went with 'I'll go ahead and kind of explain how our pricing works.'

Never stated the move-day hourly rate explicitly. Gave $190/hr for the packing day and then only a dollar range ($1,330-$1,520) for move day, so the customer has to reverse-engineer the rate. No day-of-week tier mentioned even though the booking is flexible across Sept 1/2 and she later floated 'pack Saturday, move Sunday.'
No consolidation examples in the prep speech (kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, photos off walls) — only the generic 'take a carload' tip.
No equivalents/anchoring reference (school bus, etc.) when explaining the estimate.
Disassembly/reassembly time not factored into the estimate explanation even though it applies — sectional couch that comes apart, king bed, queen bed.
Never said the confirmation email has a bolded list of key details at the top; asked the customer to verify addresses/dates/arrival window verbally instead.
Never gave business hours or how to reach the team.
Prorating explanation came out garbled and the customer had to ask 'what does that mean, prorated?'
top_strength: Textbook differentiator block delivered early and completely — No Worries damage coverage with the 60c/lb competitor contrast, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee, all before pricing. She also built the estimate transparently, naming the exact factors driving 7-8 hours (third-floor origin, parking/loading dock risk, 23rd-floor destination, 50-foot walk) instead of just dropping a number.
coaching_note: Front-load the agenda opener. She earned this booking on rapport and a well-reasoned estimate, but she opened with 'are you available to go over a few things?' and went straight into the differentiators pitch — the customer never knew the call had a shape or a length. Thirty seconds of 'I'll confirm your details, walk you through pricing and what to expect, takes about 10-15 minutes — sound good?' would have set up the whole call. Pair that with using the customer's name: he introduced himself as Babish in his first sentence and she never said it once across 21 minutes.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm and human in the back half — real empathy on the roach-infestation story ('I'm glad you're getting out of that situation'), light humor, weather small talk — but long stretches of bare 'Okay. Okay. Mm-hmm.' acknowledgment mid-call and zero use of the customer's name keep it short of Outstanding.
